title: Who gets a retention offer, framed
subtitle: What the churn prediction is for, which rung of the ladder it needs, and what it has to beat.

verdict.text: Build a logistic regression on the 8 signals known at the snapshot, and ship it only if it beats the rule `logins_30d ≤ 6` by 0.125 EUR a case on later months. The 11 columns in `model/features.py` cannot be used as listed: two use information from after the snapshot, and a third has no date to prove otherwise.

items: Decision
Who goes on the monthly retention list and gets a 25 EUR credit. Source: brief, lines 3 and 5.
Target
`churned_60d`: 1 if an active subscriber cancels within 60 days of `snapshot_date`, for each subscriber at each monthly snapshot. Source: brief, line 7; `README.md:10`; `model/extract.py:21`.
Moment
The monthly snapshot date, for all of about 40,000 active subscribers. Only what is known that day may be used. Source: brief, lines 5 and 6; `README.md:14`.
Label
Exists in history: 3,400 labelled rows, 577 churners, measured. Known 60 days after the prediction; the team accepts up to 90. Source: brief, lines 7, 8, 18 and 19.
Costs

An offer to someone who would have stayed: 25 EUR. A churner without an offer: 90 EUR, which is the 300 EUR margin times the 30 percent the offer saves. Running a model: 60,000 EUR a year. Source: brief, lines 10 to 12 and 22.
The team's bar
At least 1 in 3 churners found (recall ≥ 33.3%), and at most 6 in 10 offers wasted (precision ≥ 40%). Source: brief, lines 15 and 16.

sections.title: The ladder
sections.intro: Options from the simplest up. The hard rules come from `frame_rules.py`; an eliminated option keeps the rule that removed it.

blocks.text: **As listed, every rung is eliminated.** With the 11 columns of `model/features.py` the rule `signals-not-known` fires, because three inputs are not known at the snapshot. The frame below uses the other 8 columns, so that fact becomes true. `model/train.py` fits on the full list, so `gbt_v7` and the scores in `predictions.csv` are not evidence for any rung, and they were not used here.

blocks.title: The three columns left out
rows: `cancellation_reason`
It exists only after a cancellation, and the join has no date limit (`model/extract.py:27`). [high]
Filled on 542 rows, all 542 of them churners: 93.9% of the 577 churners.
`days_since_last_login`
It is built from the latest login ever, with no limit at the snapshot (`model/extract.py:18`, `model/features.py:23`). [high]
136 rows have a last login after their snapshot date.
`nps_last`
It joins `nps_latest` with no as-of date (`model/extract.py:26`). [med]
Cannot be checked: the column carries no date. Left out until it is joined as of the snapshot.

options.label: A lookup or a business rule
options.why: Measured on later months, the team's `logins_30d ≤ 4` finds 21.9% of churners against a bar of 33.3%. Of 75 one- and two-condition rules on logins, tickets and payment failures, only `logins_30d ≤ 6` passed on the training snapshots, and on later months it reached 39.9% precision against a floor of 40%. That is one offer short, so read it with the first assumption below.

options.label: A simple score: a few weighted signals
options.why: Open, but this rung is for missing labels or a score people must follow by hand. The brief has labels and says nobody outside the team needs to recompute a score (line 20).

options.label: A linear or logistic model
options.why: One rung above the lowest open option, for a reason from the brief: labels exist (line 18), so the weights can be learned rather than set by hand, and a Python job can call a model at list time (lines 19 and 20). It also gives a score, which the brief needs to spend the budget on those most likely to leave (line 3).

options.label: Gradient-boosted trees
options.why: Open by the rule, with 577 churners against a floor of 500. The brief names no reason to climb, and training only before the cut leaves 417 churners. This is the rung `model/train.py` builds today.

sections.title: What it would cost
sections.intro: Cost per case at the brief's 25 and 90 EUR, over all 3,400 labelled rows. Below the break-even probability of 21.7%, an offer loses money.

blocks.title: Cost per case by policy
blocks.caption: Acting on nobody is the cheaper trivial policy. The ceiling is 480,000 decisions times 15.27 EUR, or 7.33M EUR a year; the model's 60,000 EUR is 0.125 EUR a case.

blocks.text:
**Beat the rule `logins_30d ≤ 6`, at 11.90 EUR a case on later months.** The trivial baseline is the base rate of 16.97% as a score and acting on nobody at 15.27 EUR a case; the rule is stronger, so it is the one to beat. The model must reach **11.77 EUR a case or less**, since 60,000 EUR a year over 480,000 decisions is 0.125 EUR a case to earn back. A model that does not beat it is not shipped.

Later months means snapshots from 2026-04-01 on, the cut in `model/split.py`: 960 rows and 160 churners in `test.csv`.

items: The team reads "no more than 6 in 10 wasted" as approximate, or `logins_30d ≤ 6` clears 40% on a fresh later period: **a business rule**, no model and no 60,000 EUR a year.
The logistic model misses the bar, or does not beat the rule by 0.125 EUR a case on later months: **a business rule**, `logins_30d ≤ 6`.
The logistic model falls short, a later-months test shows interactions matter, and there are at least 500 churners before the cut (now 417): **gradient-boosted trees**.
Someone outside the team must recompute a score, or the list job cannot call a model: **a logistic model kept as a formula**, and trees are out.
The offer's effect differs by subscriber, so 30 percent is not flat: **still a logistic model, but the target becomes who can be saved**, which needs a randomised hold-back first (`ds-experiment`).

blocks.title: Open facts
items: The retention budget is not stated. `logins_30d ≤ 6` would mean about 6,100 offers and 153,000 EUR in credits a month, at 15.3% of 40,000 subscribers. [med]
The brief says 18 months of labelled snapshots; the extract has 12, from 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-01.
`test.csv` is not a clean holdout: 40 of its rows fall before the cut in `model/split.py`, and 150 of its customers are also in `train.csv`.
It is not stated whether a subscriber can get the credit in consecutive months.
